summary: The note surveys how rituals and superstitions persist in daily life despite scientific progress, serving as links to cultural heritage, sources of psychological comfort, and tools for social cohesion. It cites 2023 statements and events from scholars, anthropologists, educators, athletes, performers and influencers, covering transmission to younger generations, sports and entertainment, the tension between progress and tradition, and challenges in the digital age.
one_line: Rituals and superstitions endure in modern life, connecting generations, comforting people and uniting communities, with examples from fishing villages, sports, education and social media.
key_facts: On October 14, 2023, professor Sophia Ramirez of the Global Institute for Cultural Studies said rituals are "a language through which communities speak about their values, history, and bond with one another."
On September 20, 2023, sociologist Dr. James Okoye published a paper saying "Superstitions act as a shield against the uncertainties of life, albeit a symbolic one."
In Italy, placing a hat on a bed is considered bad luck, a superstition linked to the historic plague when hats of the deceased were tossed onto their beds.

On November 1, 2023, anthropologist Emma Larson observed fishers in the coastal village of Santo Pescatore touching a pendant, reciting a short prayer and marking their boats with chalk before setting sail.
On December 8, 2023, the Global Forum on Cultural Practices held a symposium on transmitting cultural practices to younger generations.
Orin Johnson from New Zealand runs the program "Roots and Wings," which teaches Maori traditions, including the Haka, to students of all backgrounds.
On December 15, 2023, Senegalese storyteller and educator Aissatou Mbodj said "With every tale I tell, I plant a seed for the future."
On September 29, 2023, an intercultural festival in Toronto featured Chinese dragon dances followed by Scandinavian midsummer pole-raising.
Cultural psychologist Dr. Anita Patel, who attended the Toronto festival, said shared rituals can serve as a bridge between communities.
Before the World Cup opening game on October 21, 2023, the Brazilian football team huddled in a collective ritual mixing prayer, motivational talk and symbolic gestures.
Broadway actress Mia Zhang taps the stage thrice before the curtain rises, a practice inherited from her mentor as a symbol of respect for the craft.
Software developer-turned-shaman Michael Ortiz calls rituals the "soul of innovation" and combines indigenous practices with modern work.
On November 28, 2023, a round-table on 'Cultural Identity in the Age of Social Media' discussed how platforms can both erode and promote traditions.
Influencer Sara Nguyen teaches young audiences about the Vietnamese practice of ancestor veneration.
